chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The prayer during travel is two rak'at, with nothing before them or after them, except for Maghrib, for after it are four rak'at. Do not leave them in residence or in travel, and there is no making up of the daytime prayer upon you, and pray the night prayer and make it up.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for shortening and combining prayers while traveling according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific application of qasr (shortening) and jam' (combining) prayers during travel, emphasizing that only the four-rak'ah prayers (Dhuhr, Asr, Isha) are shortened to two, while Maghrib remains four. It further distinguishes between obligatory makeup (qada) and voluntary night prayers (tahajjud), instructing the traveler to perform the latter but not make up missed daytime prayers, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of worship during journeys. This ruling underscores the principle of ease (taysir) in Islamic law, balancing spiritual discipline with the physical realities of travel.
